ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION
The general equations X + A = B and Y - A = B are very common to work with.
DISCUSSION
They indicate that adding or subtracting a real number from X and Y equals another real number.
For example, you may find the general equations, X + A = B and
It doesn't take algebra to know that X has to equal 3, (3+2=5) and Y has to equal 7, (7-2=5).
The answers can eventually be found using a trial and error method.
Algebra uses a systematic method to solve for X and Y.
Once you have learned this method you can solve complex problems.
Let's start with solving the linear equation X + A = B.....
The equation X + 2 = 5 means that the expression on the left
(X + 2) is the same or equal to the expression on the right (5).
The idea is to isolate the variable. This means placing X by itself on one side of the equation and all other constants on the other side.
We isolate X by cancelling the 2 from one side of the equation and placing it on the other side without changing the equality of the equation.
This is done by using the Subtraction Law.
The Subtraction Law states that a real number can be subtracted from BOTH sides of an equation without changing the equality of the equation.
Subtract 2 from both sides of this equation to isolate the variable (X).
Combining terms shows that X is equal to 3.
